about: How the pull requests, notebooks and Sherlock runs feed the kmerseek paper. Each part of the paper ("paper" below) lists the pull requests (seanome/2024-kmerseek-analysis unless repo says otherwise), notebooks, Sherlock runs and claims (ids in data/claims.json) behind it. The page joins these with data/open_prs.json (what each pull request changes, from GitHub), data/pr_review.json (review status) and data/experiments.json (each notebook's numbers). Written 2026-10-13. Two different notebooks are numbered 245; the P66/CD47 one is called 245-p66 here (notebook_aliases).

paper.name: Figure 1
paper.what: Related proteins keep their H/P pattern in runs of about 12 residues, so the seed length trades homologs reached against chance hits.
paper.number: Mean longest same-class run 12.0 residues (median 11) at 20-30% identity; 13.4% of pairs share a run of 17 or more.

paper.name: Supplementary Figure 1
paper.what: Alphabets with fewer letters carry fewer bits per letter, so each needs a longer seed: classes, bits per letter, and the k-sizes to test for all 19 alphabets.

paper.name: Alphabet figures, no figure number yet
paper.what: Bits of information per letter for all 19 alphabets, and the seven H/P alphabets differing only on C, G, P, W and Y.

paper.name: Seed reach at k*, place in the paper not decided
paper.what: No alphabet shares a seed along the alignment in more than 5.6% of Pfam seed pairs at 20-30% identity.
paper.number: mmseqs12 is highest (2,060 of 37,085 pairs); protein20 reaches 4.9%, the 2-3 letter alphabets 0.47-0.85%.

paper.name: Figure files saved as 256-colour PNGs
paper.what: pf.save and shrink_png, and 321 committed PNGs re-saved with 256 colours.

paper.name: CED-9 and BCL2
paper.what: The known homolog pair, the gold standard. They share the BH1 region.
paper.number: BCL2 is among CED-9's hits for 13 of 19 alphabets but never ranks better than 213 of 18,064 human proteins hit; best E-value 1,955. Only 4 of 19 alphabets agree on BCL2's best spot.

paper.name: P66 and CD47
paper.what: A published claim that the Borreliella burgdorferi protein P66 mimics human CD47. The stretch case.
paper.number: CD47's best rank is 166 of 18,775, best E-value 707. P66's fold scores below all 20 unrelated immunoglobulin domains against CD47 (TM-score 0.342).

paper.name: BHF
paper.what: Botryllus histocompatibility factor, the application: BLAST and HMMER find nothing for it.
paper.number: By E-value, 3 of 61 settings beat 95% of dipeptide-shuffled copies of BHF, against 3.1 expected by chance.

paper.name: Hero examples and case gallery
paper.what: Short Swiss-Prot features that kmerseek places on a related protein, with figures and pages for all 183 cases.

paper.name: H/P agreement in related proteins
paper.what: How often H/P classes agree at aligned positions of Pfam seed pairs at 20-30% identity, against chance.
paper.number: 73.9 of 100 aligned positions agree, against 51.4 by chance; H/P carries 0.162 bits per aligned position, the 20 amino acids 0.251.

paper.name: H/P against BLOSUM62
paper.what: Evidence per aligned position for every kmerseek alphabet against BLOSUM62.
paper.number: H/P gives about half BLOSUM62's evidence; no alphabet beats BLOSUM62 (0 of 108 scorings). hp_thomas_dill2 leads exact matching at the SCOPe fold level (1.78 times protein20).

paper.name: Agreement and k-sizes for 19 alphabets
paper.what: Cohen's kappa and usable k for all 19 alphabets, and the k-sizes to test per alphabet from k_min to k_max.

paper.name: Bits a seed carries
paper.what: Bits an exact reduced-alphabet seed carries, against the bits a search of this database size needs.

paper.name: Seeds that allow mismatches
paper.what: Seeds with mismatches on CED-9/BCL2 and P66/CD47.

paper.name: Dark proteins
paper.what: Proteins with no phmmer, jackhmmer or MMseqs2 hit in Swiss-Prot once the query's own clade is removed.
paper.number: The best setting reaches 12-26% of dark proteins at E < 1, against 38-73% of proteins that have a hit. The reached ones are enriched for compositional bias (human: 58.7% against 36.2%).

paper.name: Pfam domains, kmerseek against aligners
paper.what: Held-out half of 21,915 human Pfam instance by species rows.
paper.number: No held-out domain is placed only by kmerseek; in 183 cases kmerseek's boundary is tighter.

paper.name: ELM short linear motifs
paper.what: Moving ELM motif labels across species.
paper.number: kmerseek places no motif that all the other tools miss, in 8 species.

paper.name: Recall against domain length
paper.what: Share of Pfam domains placed, by domain length.
paper.number: Best setting: 0.365 of domains under 50 residues, 0.060 of domains of 200 or more; phmmer and Foldseek rise with length.

paper.name: SCOPe40 with kmerseek 0.4
paper.what: 19 alphabets, every k from k_min to k_max, six search settings; then k below k_min, by identity band.
paper.number: Best family AUC 0.122 (hsdm17, k = 5) against 0.403 for MMseqs2, measured against all true pairs. The best k sits at the bottom of the tested range.

paper.name: Time-split Pfam test
paper.what: Would kmerseek have placed domains that Pfam added between release 33.1 (2020) and 38.2 (2026)?

paper.name: Combining settings
paper.what: Three ways to combine alphabet-ksize pairs (intersection, best of n, consensus vote), against the single best pair, phmmer and a Kyte-Doolittle scan.

paper.name: Shuffled-query check
paper.what: One dipeptide shuffle of each of the 998 queries, searched against zebrafish.
paper.number: 335 calls at E < 10 for shuffled queries against 891 for real ones (38%); at E < 1, 22 against 673 (3%).

paper.name: DisProt region transfer
paper.what: Moving a DisProt function label onto a disordered region of another protein.

paper.name: Deep-twilight controls
paper.what: Label transfer on globins, lysozymes and cystatins.

paper.name: Other benchmark pull requests

paper.status: no result in the progress summary

paper.name: Ohnolog split or narrow
paper.what: Whether vertebrate gene copies from the two genome duplications split their ancestor's cell types or one copy narrows, with Botryllus as the ancestor stand-in.

steps.name: Look again
steps.when: When you sit down to review, open these first: you left comments, and new commits came after.

steps.name: Runs to read
steps.when: When a Sherlock run finishes, read it in its notebook before reviewing the pull request.
steps.rule: a run in the queue belongs to it

steps.name: Figure PRs
steps.when: When step 1 is done, review the pull requests behind the paper figures.

steps.name: Example PRs
steps.when: When the figure pull requests are reviewed, review the ones behind the three examples, lowest in each stack first.
steps.rule: feeds one of the three examples

steps.name: Evidence PRs
steps.when: When the examples are reviewed, review the alphabet evidence and benchmark pull requests.
steps.rule: feeds another part of the paper

steps.name: kmerseek PRs
steps.when: When you switch to the search engine, review these seanome/kmerseek pull requests.

steps.name: Decide
steps.when: When the rest is reviewed, decide for each of these: fold it into a part of the paper, keep it as a tool, or close it.
steps.rule: feeds no part of the paper yet
